newsitem.title: MEXICO: Six Mexicans killed in Chiapas land dispute.
newsitem.headline: Six Mexicans killed in Chiapas land dispute.

text.p: Six people were killed when a land dispute erupted into a shootout between peasants and paramilitary supporters of a local political boss in the southern state of Chiapas, officials said on Wednesday.

The gunfight flared on Sunday when peasant supporters of the leftist Party of the Democratic Revolution (PRD) tried to claim land near Pueblo Nuevo Solistahuacan, 55 miles (90 km) north of this state capital. News of the battle reached state officials late on Tuesday.

"The peasants arrived on the morning of June 8 armed with AR-15 rifles and were greeted with gunfire from 'white guard' (paramilitary) gunmen hired by a local landowner," Pueblo Nuevo mayor Carlos Rojas told Reuters.

Rojas said three peasants and three gunmen were killed in the incident, which followed years of conflict in the area after peasants took over land belonging to Pacifico Rojas Lopez, owner of the "El Porvenir" ranch.
There has been a series of recent battles between radical peasants and local political bosses in the state, one of Mexico's poorest and home to the mostly Mayan Zapatista rebels.

Landless Indian peasants launched a wave of land takeovers in the months after the Zapatista's January 1994 uprising against the Mexican government. The Zapatistas have since been in peace talks but the underlying land conflict simmers.
Local peasant leaders told Reuters they planned to press their claims to the land, which they said the owner planned to sell to local supporters of the ruling Institutional Revolutionary Party (PRI).
"The situation in Pueblo Nuevo is very tense," said Gustavo Zarate, head of the State Assembly of the Chiapas Peoples, an umbrella group for local peasant organisations.
